title: secp256k1-ecdlp: plain parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points, conservatively charged

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and Q=[x]P with the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the plain parallel Pollard rho in proof.md (1024-adding walk, 76-bit distinguished points, 2^32 walks with batched inversion, uniform segment restarts, 2^82-step segment cap and a fully charged completion phase) recovers x with probability at least 0.40 using at most 2^(12903/100) total target-group-operation equivalents under protected C=1000. Each walk step is charged as one batched incomplete affine addition plus at most 1000 scalar instructions; preprocessing, restarts, storage, sorting, collision resolution and verification are charged. Peak memory is below 2^63.01 bytes; preprocessing is below 2^25 equivalents and included in total; nonuniform advice is zero bytes (log convention 0). The success bound relies on the disclosed random-walk heuristic H for r-adding walks, supported by literature and toy runs of the same algorithm. No negation map or endomorphism is used, so there are no fruitless cycles. Classical single-target cold attack; analytic bound, not an executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Run the same parallel r-adding rho as proof.md (DP segments, uniform restarts, segment cap, completion phase, sort-and-match, verification) on small prime-order y^2=x^3+7 curves; measure whether a repeated element occurs among the phase-1 visited points and compare that rate with 1-exp(-k1^2/(2n/(1-2/R))) (heuristic H), and report full-algorithm success and solved/repeat counts. Toy-scale evidence only; the verifier allows one initial run, the full pooled table with seeds is in proof.md.
